title: Chapter 6. The Ascertainment of Sri Nityananda and Gaurachandra
html:
A theological chapter: Nityananda and Chaitanya as Balarama and Krishna; Ananga Manjari and Jahnava; the power of the holy name; scriptural testimonies to Gauranga's descent (pp. 51–54)

[p. 51]

1Glory, glory to Nityananda, the form of the descent!
Glory, glory to him who is in essence the friend of Radha's life!

2Glory, glory to him who delights in the rasa dance1!
Glory, glory to the preacher of the love of Radha and Krishna!

3Nityananda-Rama is the beloved body of Chaitanya:
day and night he fulfils Chaitanya's desires.

4Who can tell of the love of Chaitanya and Nitai?
Only the thousand-mouthed Lord2, if he had the power.

5The love and affection of these two only they themselves know,
and those who have received the mercy of both.

6Glory, glory to Nityananda! Glory to the Merciful One,
by merely taking whose name bhakti is attained!

7Such are the pastimes Nityananda Raya performs;
only a few fortunate ones are able to see them.

8The wretched unbeliever does not accept this —
the rod of Yama zealously punishes him.

9What have I to do with him — let him die or not!
My mind always remains at the Prabhu's feet.

10When [the Lord] is within the range of the manifest world, he is called "manifest" (prakata); when beyond the manifest world, he is called "unmanifest" (aprakata).

11Appearance as revelation (sphurti) is a mark of his true nature:
thus the devotees understand the Lord's pastimes.

12In sankirtana he is revealed and appears to the devotees,
and in the form of Virachandra — with all the marks of his true nature.

13Internal, external and marginal [energies] — so it is named3;
no one knows this except the intimate ones (antaranga).

14One in whose mind the [embodied]4 goddess Bhakti awakens
knows revelation and appearance by the marks of his true nature.

15Through knowledge, action and yoga, through the Vedas, this is not attained:
Chaitanya Gosani is within the reach of bhakti alone.

16In the Kali age the merciful Nitai and Chaitanya
descended, compassionate to living beings.

17Lifting my face and raising both arms, I say, brothers:
in the Kali age there is no other dharma or duty.

18Appearing himself, he proclaimed the holy name:
take that name, all of you, and you will cross over [the ocean of existence].

19In the Kali age Krishna will be won over by the power of the name;
there is no love higher than this, no [higher] rasa of bhakti.

20Whoever has taken the name has conquered Krishna:
truly, truly, Krishna is bound to him.

21The name is Brahman, the name is Brahman, the name is Brahman in truth!
Krishna and Krishna's name are two, yet they are one reality.

22Krishna and Krishna's name are never different:
the name and Krishna's body are non-different, say the Vedas.

23Take the name with love, do not neglect it —
truly, truly, you will obtain the mercy of the son of Nanda Ghosha5.

24Without loving devotion no aim is achieved:
shaving the head does not avert the rod of Yama.

25The name of Hari is the king of mantras; chant it, all living beings!
This is the fifth goal of life6, as we hear in all the shastras.

26Nityananda in the form of the guru, Advaita in the form of the Vaishnava,
Sri Krishna Chaitanya in the form [of God]: such is the view of the shastras.

27There is no one else to give the mantra of Radha and Krishna;
whoever regards them as different is ruined.

28In the Kali age the mantra-guru and the instructing guru
are, in essence, Nityananda, Gaurachandra and Advaita.

29The shelter, the object and the stimulus [of emotion]7, becoming one,
appeared in the Kali age for the sake of living beings.

[p. 52]

30Whoever accepts this is truly wise;
whoever does not accept this is a heretic and a fool.

31To this day Gaura Raya performs these pastimes;
only a few fortunate ones are able to see them.

32The wretched unbeliever does not accept this —
the rod of Yama zealously punishes him.

33What have I to do with him — let him die or not!
My mind always remains at the Prabhu's feet.

34One endowed with every virtue but lacking devotion to Nityananda —
I will never look upon such a sinner, devoid of merit.

35But one devoid of every virtue, bereft of all dharma,
who loves Nityananda — he is honoured everywhere.

36Whoever remembers Nityananda for even half a moment,
the dust of his feet I make the ornament of my head.

37Now hear of the greatness of Nityananda,
the Prabhu to whom the four Vedas cannot set a limit.

38When [the Lord] is within the range of the manifest world, he is called "manifest";
when beyond the manifest world, he is called "unmanifest".

39Appearance as revelation is a mark of his true nature:
thus the devotees understand the Lord's pastimes.

40In sankirtana he is revealed and appears to the devotees,
and in the form of Virachandra — with all the marks of his true nature.

41Those whom the Vedas sing of as Krishna and Balarama
are, in the Kali age, the two: Chaitanya and Nitai.

42For Krishna's happiness there is one Prabhu, Balarama:
taking every form, he fulfils Krishna's desires.

43In Vrindavana Sri Balarama is Krishna's manifestation:
he gives joy to Krishna's heart — this is his desire.

44Thus [it is said] in the Brahmanda Purana, in the Dialogue of the Earth and Shesha8:
"In Goloka is two-armed Krishna, whose form is being, consciousness and bliss;
this one is his manifested form, his second body."

45In the same:
"Only the colour differs; in their own nature they are one;
lustre, beauty, majesty — all is alike, there is no doubt."9

46Nityananda is that Balarama-Sankarshana,
who is worshipped with the fifteen-syllable mantra10.

47In the kama-gayatri and the meditation mantra I see one form:
Krishna and Balarama are but one essence.

48Sometimes he plays in male form,
sometimes, becoming the supreme Prakriti, he performs the pastimes of rasa.

49In the same:
"He by whom Rama has the nature of Krishna, […] in Goloka,
where in Vrindavana, in the grove, in play with Radhika […] —
this is Balarama in male form, who nourishes the pastimes of the two,
a special [manifestation] of Krishnachandra, the leader of the games in the cow pastures.
All principles — creation and the rest — are endowed with [his] energies;
[she] is the one joined with Radhika's rasa, endowed with Krishna's energy."11

50In him are majesty and sweetness; he is the abode of the rasa of bhakti:
in this sense the Puranas extol Balarama.

51In the same:
"'Bala' — [because] in all deeds [he acts] by his own strength, […] pure;
therefore he is called Balabhadra — this I have said briefly, in passing.
The syllable 'ra' is Srimati Radha, the syllable 'ma' is Madhusudana:
from the union of the two forms the name 'Rama' arises."12

52That Balarama took the form of Nityananda;
that Krishna descended in Kali as Chaitanya.

[p. 53]

53Thus [it is said] in the Upapurana:
"Nitya (the Eternal) is Sri Radhika, Ananda (Bliss) is the form of Krishna;
from the union of the two forms he is called Nityananda."13

54Krishna says: "I am the Lord of all, the refuge of all;
if I do not deliver the living beings, what course will they have?"

55Thus [it is said] in the Srimad Bhagavatam:
"I alone existed in the beginning, nothing else — neither the manifest nor the unmanifest nor the supreme;
afterwards too I am, and all this is I, and what remains is also I."14

56Thus [it is said] in the Naradiya [Purana]:
"Dwellers of heaven, be born on earth in the form of devotees!
In Kali, when sankirtana begins, I shall become the son of Shachi."15

57In the Kali age living beings have short lives and little merit:
delivering such beings, I shall make the Kali age blessed.

58Thus [it is said] in the Vamana Purana:
"Pure golden, tall of body, born on the bank of the Three-streamed16,
compassionate, embracing kirtana — so shall I appear in the Kali age."

59In the same:
"All those covered by the dreadful darkness of Kali, bereft of right conduct,
I, born from the womb of Shachi, shall deliver, O Narada."

60By the sacrifice of Hari-nama making all pure17,
I shall give joy to the devotees, remaining hidden.

61Thus [it is said] in the Srimad Bhagavatam:
"O Mahapurusha, you protect the dharma suited to each yuga;
in Kali you are hidden, therefore [you are called] Triyuga."18

62That Krishna, together with his companions and his chief Prakriti,
descended and gave love to the living beings.

63Thus [it is said] in the Bhagavatam:
"Him who [utters] the syllables 'Krish-na', not black in lustre, with his companions, associates, weapons and intimates,
the intelligent worship with sacrifices consisting chiefly of sankirtana."19

64Sri Chaitanya is Krishna, Nityananda is Balarama:
taking two forms20, they fulfilled every desire.

65The object (vishaya-alambana) is Krishna, the shelter (ashraya) is Radhika;
without the shelter the object cannot be tasted21.

66Therefore, displaying Radha's emotion and lustre,
[the Lord] appeared, named Gauranga Sri Hari.

67Thus [it is said] in the Skanda Purana:
"Krishna within, Gaura without, displaying the splendour of his limbs and associates22 —
in Kali [the wise], by sankirtana and the like, take refuge in Krishna Chaitanya."23

68Ananga Manjari is a portion of Balarama's female nature;
she is entitled to serve Radha's person.

69Without shakti one cannot serve Radha's person:
becoming Radha's younger sister, she serves Krishna.

70Taking Radha's emotion, Gauranga Sri Hari
descended in the Kali age, compassionate to living beings.

71Thus [it is said] in the Brahma Purana:
"In Kali, in its first junction period24, the consort of Lakshmi will appear —
a sannyasi of golden form, abiding near the Daru-brahman25."

72Thus [it is said] in the Garuda Purana:
"Pure, golden, tall of body, born on the bank of the Ganga,
compassionate, embracing kirtana — so shall I appear in the Kali age."

73Thus [it is said] in the Kurma Purana:
"For the deliverance of embodied beings burnt by Kali26,
in the first junction period of Kali he will be born among the twice-born."

74Thus [it is said] in the Devi Purana, in the dialogue of Shiva and Narada:
"In Kali, at the junction, the Lord will appear […];
Purushottama will be born in a family of peaceful twice-born."27

75Thus [it is said] in the Srimad Bhagavatam (Garga's words to the king of Vraja):
"He who takes a body in each yuga had three colours —
white, red and yellow; now he has become black."28

[p. 54]

76Thus [it is said] in the Sri Mahabharata:
"Gold-coloured, with golden limbs, beautifully formed, adorned with [sandal-paste] armlets,
having taken sannyasa, even-minded, peaceful, devoted to steadfastness and peace."29

77Thus the Vedas, shastras and Puranas say:
the hidden descent in Kali is made plain in the Vedas.

78Whoever does not accept this is a wicked and evil person;
what need have we of such foolish people?

79Whoever is averse to Nityananda and Gaurachandra —
the faces of such people I will never look upon.

80Ananga Manjari is a portion of Balarama's female nature,
a manifestation of Radhika, a companion of Krishna.

81That Rama is Nityananda, Jahnava is Ananga:
differing in their manifestations, they sport with Krishna.

82Ananga Manjari always performs these pastimes,
sometimes with Rama, sometimes sporting with Govinda.

83Nityananda's form is Chaitanya's own self-manifestation:
in the form of the guru who gives the mantra, he is revealed as the mantra itself.

84Whoever makes a difference between such a Nityananda and Chaitanya,
for him are special, unbroken torments of hell.

85Fixing this truth firmly in my heart:
[…]30 — Nityananda-chandra and Gaurahari.

86May my mind always dwell on Nityananda and Gaurachandra:
this remembrance is all my sadhana and all my perfection.

87Nityananda and Krishna Chaitanya are my Prabhus;
the lotus feet of the two brothers I will never forget.

88Will such a day come when I shall see Chaitanya and Nityananda
surrounded on all sides by crowds of devotees?

89Hoping for the feet of Sri Virachandra Prabhu,
Vrindavana Dasa tells the Spreading of the Lineage.

Thus ends the sixth chapter, named "The Ascertainment of Sri Nityananda and Gaurachandra", in the Madhya-lila of the Spreading of the Lineage of Sri Nityananda Prabhu.

Translator's notes

Notes

  1. The copies have "rā līlā"; restored as "rāsa līlā" (the rasa pastime, the circle dance).
  2. The thousand-mouthed Lord is Ananta-Shesha, the thousand-headed serpent who eternally sings the Lord's glories; he is himself a manifestation of Balarama, i.e. of Nityananda.
  3. The three energies of the Lord in Gaudiya Vaishnava theology: internal (antaranga, spiritual), external (bahiranga, material) and marginal (tatastha, to which the living beings belong).
  4. The first word of the line is unclear (A "muchi", B "mupti"); read as "mūrti", "embodied". "supta" is also possible: "the goddess Bhakti, dormant [in the heart], awakens".
  5. The copies have "kṛpā kridne / kṛpā pavipena"; read as "kṛpā pāivena", "you will obtain mercy".
  6. Beyond the four traditional goals of life (dharma, artha, kama, moksha), Gaudiya Vaishnavas name prema, love of God, as the fifth and highest.
  7. Terms of rasa theory: ashraya, the "shelter" or bearer of the emotion (the devotee); alambana (vishaya), its object (Krishna); uddipana, what excites the emotion.
  8. The Sanskrit verses in this chapter are heavily corrupted in the printed text (both through OCR and, apparently, in the typesetting itself); the translation follows the restored readings. The Dialogue of the Earth and Shesha (Dharani-Shesha-samvada) was mentioned in ch. 5.
  9. Restored as "varṇa-mātraṁ pṛthak caiva svarūpeṇaikam eva hi / kānti-lāvaṇyam aiśvaryaṁ sarvakaṁ na saṁśayaḥ".
  10. The fifteen-syllable mantra is one of the mantras for worshipping Krishna/Balarama; the kama-gayatri (couplet 47) is a mantra used in Gaudiya Vaishnava initiation.
  11. The verse (six lines) is badly corrupted in both copies: in the first two lines only isolated words are clear (A "golakājjādi-vākavaraḥ", "rādhikā kuca…"); the rest is restored as "pumān sa balarāmo 'yaṁ dvaya-līlādi-poṣakaḥ / viśeṣaḥ kṛṣṇacandrasya goṣṭha-krīḍādi-nāyakaḥ / nānā-sṛṣṭy-ādikaṁ tattvaṁ sarvaṁ śaktibhir yutam / rādhikā-rāsa-yuktā yā kṛṣṇa-śakti-samanvitā". The translation of the last lines is conjectural.
  12. The first line is corrupt ("valeti sarva kārye svavale vānaodra nirmala"); what is clear has been translated. The second half derives the name "Rama" from "Ra" (Radha) and "Ma" (Madhusudana, Krishna).
  13. The copies have "anenda"; restored as "ānandaḥ" (nityā śrī-rādhikā caiva ānandaḥ kṛṣṇa-vigrahaḥ) — a play on words: Nitya + Ananda = Nityananda.
  14. Bhagavatam 2.9.32 (from the chatuh-shloki, the four verses spoken by the Lord to Brahma).
  15. A well-known verse attributed to the Narada Purana; the first half is distorted in the copies.
  16. The Three-streamed (Trisrota) is the Ganga.
  17. The copies have "yajjate kari sava puṇya"; understood as "by the sacrifice of Hari-nama making all pure (righteous)".
  18. Bhagavatam 7.9.38 (Prahlada's prayer); only the second half and part of the first are given. The name "Triyuga" ("[manifest] in three yugas") is explained by the Lord's coming hidden in Kali.
  19. Bhagavatam 11.5.32. In the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition "krishna-varna" is understood as "uttering the syllables 'Krish-na'" (or "black within"), and "tvisha akrishna" as "not black in lustre", i.e. golden.
  20. The copies have "vu munḍi" (A), "mūrti" (B, beginning of the line lost); read as "dui mūrti", "two forms".
  21. Terms of rasa theory: vishaya-alambana, the object of love (Krishna); ashraya-alambana, the bearer of love (Radha). To taste Radha's love Krishna takes on her emotion — hence the descent of Gauranga.
  22. "Anga", "limbs"; in Gaudiya Vaishnava exegesis also his closest associates.
  23. This verse is widely known as the opening verse of Jiva Gosvami's Tattva-sandarbha; here it is attributed to the Skanda Purana.
  24. Sandhya, the transitional period at the beginning of a yuga.
  25. Daru-brahman, "Brahman in wood", i.e. the wooden deity of Jagannatha at Puri.
  26. The copies have "tamobhūtāṁ"; understood as "tanu-bhṛtām", "of embodied beings".
  27. The first line apparently has a gap (the metre is incomplete).
  28. Bhagavatam 10.8.13: Garga Muni, at Krishna's name-giving, tells Nanda of the colours of his descents in the various yugas. Gaudiya Vaishnavas take "yellow" (pita) as pointing to the golden Gauranga.
  29. Cited as a verse of the Vishnu-sahasra-nama (Mahabharata, Anushasana-parva); the epithets are understood to point to Gauranga, golden and a sannyasi.
  30. The beginning of the line is illegible (A "aśnrākma", B "a+pannākma"); possibly "āpanāra", "my own [refuge/treasure]".
